parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal statute, but police abuse at identity checks and arbitrary vagrancy/public-order arrests are documented in a 2025 UN submission, corroborating 2016 blackmail/arrests and 2020 violent detentions. No LGR means foreign-document mismatch cannot be aligned locally and becomes an identity-check encounter. No gender-identity anti-discrimination recourse, LGBTIQ organisations cannot register openly, and asylum SOPs protect claimants, not visitors. No universal facility/ward rule or capital/organised campaign is documented, and dated incidents are old, holding this above severe/high-risk targeting, but state-tolerated police targeting without working remedy keeps it at 0.35-level.

entry_documents.exposure: Law forbids changing legal gender; visitor documents cannot be aligned locally and identity checks are documented harassment site.
entry_documents.protection: Not documented. Asylum interview SOPs naming gender identity do not govern visitor entry.
entry_documents.interaction: Document/presentation mismatch at a check can trigger questioning, harassment or public-order arrest.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Arbitrary arrests on vagrancy/public-order grounds and violent detentions reported 2020; custody placement and conditions not documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Identity-check encounter can escalate to detention, with no documented visitor remedy.

care_services.exposure: Visitor-specific emergency care, ward placement and medication carriage not documented.
care_services.protection: Resident health policy states equal entitlement regardless of gender/orientation, but is not shown operating for visitors.
care_services.interaction: Unknown whether care encounter would out visitor or affect treatment.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: 2016 harassment, blackmail and arrests under public-order/morality laws; official non-engagement posture; stigma and taboo.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Asylum/humanitarian SOPs and 2022 refugee grant name gender identity, but only for claimants.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: General public-order powers are documented lever against trans people despite no trans-specific offence.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Harassment by neighbours and police reported historically; singer stopped on street after hotel show in capital.
street_violence_police_response.protection: One minister publicly backed a singer in 2019; no documented prosecution or victim remedy.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police are documented as perpetrators in checks, so calling police does not reliably protect.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No gender-identity anti-discrimination claim; LGBTIQ organisations cannot register openly; 2024 NGO law raises association concerns.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Not documented as effective for a visitor facing harassment, extortion or arbitrary arrest.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Border screening, facility rules, custody placement, frequency of current violence and minor-specific risks remain unknown, not safe.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: repeated police stops at identity checks, coercive demands/blackmail and arrests without documented discipline or refunds; shops may serve visitors but official suspicion dominates. This dossier has less documented payment pattern, hence slightly varied, but same unremedied targeting tier.

Lower than this case: 0.25-A documents repeated raids, multi-day detention and birth-sex custody sexual harassment. Here arbitrary arrests and violent detentions are documented, but no custody placement, raid frequency or sustained detention pattern is sourced, so not as severe.

Higher than this case: 0.55-B has hostile service treatment but mediators secure readmissions/refunds and police convict an assailant. Here no visitor-facing remedy operating is documented and police themselves are documented abusers, so rating is materially below 0.55.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: no trans-specific offence or facility ban is documented, but the live interaction is document mismatch -> identity check -> harassment/arbitrary public-order arrest, with no gender-identity anti-discrimination recourse and closed civil society. Asylum protections benefit claimants, not tourists, and do not cancel police exposure. Old dated incidents are weakly probative of current frequency, yet the 2025 submission provides recent corroboration of the same practice. Unknown border, custody, ward and minor risks cannot be treated as safety. This is state-tolerated targeting without effective remedy, aligning near 0.35-C, moderated by absence of documented imprisonment/custody pattern.
